header.running_head: Dispatching the Sahabah (RA) to Various Lands for Teaching

blocks.text: Marthad (RA), who was a close friend of Hadhrat Hamzah bin Abdul Muttalib (RA). The Hadith then continues to speak about the Battle of Rajee. [^1]
Rasulullaah ﷺ Sends Hadhrat Ali (RA) and Hadhrat Abu Ubaydah bin Jarraah (RA) to Yemen

Hadhrat Ali (RA) narrates, "Some people from Yemen once came to Rasulullaah ﷺ saying, 'Please send to us someone who will help us develop an understanding of the Deen, who will teach us the Sunnah and judge between us by the Book of Allaah.' Rasulullaah ﷺ said, 'O Ali! Go to the people of Yemen, develop an understanding of Deen amongst them, teach them the Sunnah and judge between them by the Book of Allaah.' I responded by saying, 'But the people of Yemen are a foolish bunch who will bring me cases about which I will have no knowledge.' Rasulullaah ﷺ placed his hand on my chest and reassured me saying, 'Go. Allaah shall guide your heart and make your tongue unwavering.' (By the blessings of this du'aa) Until this day, I have never doubted any judgement I have passed between two persons." [^2]

Hadhrat Anas (RA) narrates that some people from Yemen once approached Rasulullaah ﷺ with the request, "Do send with us someone who will teach us the Qur'aan." Rasulullaah ﷺ took hold of the hand of Hadhrat Abu Ubaydah bin Jarraah (RA) and sent him with them saying, "This is the most trustworthy person of this Ummah." [^3] Another narration states that the people of Yemen requested Rasulullaah ﷺ for someone who would teach them the Sunnah and Islaam. [^4]
Rasulullaah ﷺ Sends Hadhrat Amr bin Hazam (RA), Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari (RA) and Hadhrat Mu'aadh bin Jabal (RA) to Yemen

blocks.narrator: Hadhrat Abu Bakr bin Muhammad bin Amr bin Hazam
blocks.text: Hadhrat Abu Bakr bin Muhammad bin Amr bin Hazam said, "Here with us is the letter (of appointment) that Rasulullaah ﷺ had written for Hadhrat Amr bin Hazam (RA) when Rasulullaah ﷺ sent him to Yemen to educate the people (in Islaam), to teach them the Sunnah and to collect their zakaah. The letter was an undertaking from Hadhrat Amr bin Hazam (RA) and a briefing. The letter stated: "In the name of Allaah, the Most Kind, the Most Merciful. This is a letter from Allaah and His Rasool ﷺ.
O you who have Imaan, fulfil the undertakings you make.
Ibn Jareer, as quoted in Muntakhab Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.5 Pg.37).
